newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE RATES STEADY IN LIQUID MONEY MARKET.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE RATES STEADY IN LIQUID MONEY MARKET.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted little changed at their overnight levels in early Tuesday trade, dealers said.
"It looks like the market is fairly liquid today. We opened with a surplus and rates are still depressed," commented one dealer.
Discount houses were on Tuesday buying central bank paper at the 22.49 percent set at last Thursday's weekly auction and were selling them at 22 percent in the market.
NCD bills redeemable after 30, 60 and 90 days were buying and selling at 23.50 and 22.75 percent, little changed from Monday's 23.50 and 22.50 percent.
Bankers acceptances were also quoted stable at 22.50 and 22.25 percent, while call money held on to Monday's 22 percent.
The central Reserve Bank said the market opened in surplus of Z$522 million, a recovery from Monday's Z$48 million start-off shortage.
